title: Lit Circles
summary: Four-week literature circles for grades 9–12: groups read the book they choose, prepare with reading strategies, discuss, assess each other and reflect.

steps.caption: The student view. Each group reads its own book, one week at a time.
Every week starts with a question worth thinking about.
Students choose how to prepare: close reading, connections, or a journal.
They pick two reading strategies that fit what they noticed.
One strategy at a time, with a checklist beside the writing. It saves as they type.

steps.text: Buck is stolen from his comfortable home in California and sold to men who take him north to the Yukon.

steps.caption: Then the group meets to discuss, assesses each other, and reflects.
The teacher dashboard. Every step of every week is a tile.
Red numbers are work waiting for you. ↻ means a student redid something after you graded it.
The rubric is right on the grading screen.
Click a score, then add a comment. Ready-made comments are one click away.
Everything saves on its own. Push grades to Canvas when you’re ready.
